current_leader.name: Subscription grace-period cost/recovery optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: subscription renewal fails -> app-store billing-retry/grace-period event appears -> developer must choose/maintain a platform-level grace-period duration while service continues -> longer grace increases recovery probability but can incur incremental service/AI/content cost for subscribers who never recover -> use observed recovery curves plus marginal service cost to recommend the economically optimal grace-period configuration -> protect net subscription margin rather than gross recovery alone
current_leader.why_survived: The underlying money flow is large and current 2026 subscription-app data shows billing failures are a major involuntary-churn source, especially on Google Play. Apple exposes 3/16/28-day grace choices and an App Store Connect API PATCH endpoint to change grace configuration. Google permits configurable grace/account-hold windows and reports materially better recovery with longer recovery periods. Existing tools strongly cover dunning, subscriber-level messaging, retry-state analytics and recovery workflows, but this search did not find a dominant product whose narrow job is to optimize the store-level grace-period duration from each app's actual recovery hazard curve versus marginal cost-to-serve. This is materially different from generic failed-payment recovery because it optimizes a provider-native configuration rather than replacing retry/dunning rails.
strongest_evidence: RevenueCat State of Subscription Apps 2026 reports that roughly a third of Google Play subscription cancellations are involuntary billing failures and about 15% on the App Store in its dataset.
Google reported that extending the decline-recovery period from 30 to 60 days produced an average 10% reduction in involuntary churn for renewals.
Apple allows Billing Grace Period choices of 3, 16, or 28 days and exposes PATCH /v1/subscriptionGracePeriods/{id} to modify the opt-in status and duration.
RevenueCat exposes BILLING_ISSUE/grace-period events and recovery events, so recovery curves are machine-readable without owning payment processing.

Current dunning vendors such as RedChurn, Recurflux and Rezoki operate on billing events and messaging/recovery, but the search did not identify an exact optimizer for the app-level grace-duration configuration itself.
current_leader.closest_threat: The strongest first-party threat is that longer grace may be an obvious default for low-marginal-cost apps, reducing the optimization problem to 'choose the longest period'. Google already enables grace by default and encourages longer recovery windows. The wedge is strongest only for high-variable-cost subscription services, such as AI/compute/content-cost apps, where unrecovered users can consume meaningful cost during grace. Existing subscription analytics/dunning platforms could also add this recommendation cheaply.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read App Store/Google Play or RevenueCat billing-issue and renewal events plus per-user or cohort cost-to-serve; estimate recovery probability by day and expected net value of 3/16/28-day (Apple) or available Google recovery-window settings; output a configuration recommendation and expected incremental net margin. Initially no payment control and no subscriber messaging. With explicit authorization, apply Apple configuration through App Store Connect API after recommendation validation.
current_leader.monetization: Per configuration optimization cycle or a capped share of measured incremental net margin versus the prior configuration. Performance pricing remains uncertain because Apple configuration is app-wide and causal attribution across periods can be noisy; a small success/event fee or low flat fee tied to recovered net margin may be stronger.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Objective attribution is weaker than detection: Apple applies one grace setting across an app, making clean contemporaneous A/B testing difficult, and for low-cost apps the economically dominant answer may simply be maximum grace. The next test must prove a meaningful cohort of high-COGS subscription apps where the optimal duration is non-trivial and where configuration changes generate measurable net-margin deltas large enough to support a fee.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify the tradeoff for high-variable-cost mobile subscriptions: obtain or find public recovery-by-day curves and typical marginal cost-to-serve for AI, compute-heavy, licensed-content or other costly apps; model when 3 vs 16 vs 28 days changes expected net margin. Then search exact competitors for 'grace period optimizer', 'billing retry duration optimizer' and store-configuration recommendation products. Kill if longest grace is economically dominant across realistic cost structures or if an incumbent already optimizes the setting.

runner_ups.reason: Still has clean quota/reset triggers and measurable overage avoidance, but no single high-value non-AI/non-enrichment vertical with proven leakage and easy read-only scheduling has yet been found.
Expiry is real, but multi-provider messaging routers already own the routing decision and can absorb expiry-awareness.
Excellent machine-readable tariff/price signals and dollar deltas, but mature battery/DER/EV optimization software and APIs already optimize timing directly.

rejections_or_failed_attacks.reason: Current RevenueCat-integrated and store-specific vendors already handle retry-state detection, dunning, deep links and win-back; only the configuration optimization micro-decision remains potentially open.
Current tracking APIs already push Last Free Date/available-for-pickup events explicitly to reduce demurrage; obvious alerting/scheduling wedge is occupied.
Current finance-grade products calculate and evidence payout splits without moving money; generic reconciliation is occupied.
Current price-signal APIs and DER/battery optimizers already make operating decisions price-aware; generic timing wedge is mature.
The forfeiture event can be real, but intervention depends on employment termination and employee purchasing behavior, with low repeat frequency per person and weak autonomous monetization.

new_search_rules: Provider-native configurable recovery windows can be opportunities only when the financially optimal setting is non-obvious; if 'maximum grace' dominates for nearly all customers, the wedge collapses to a checkbox.

Separate gross revenue recovery from net-margin recovery. For high-variable-cost digital services, allowing unpaid users continued access has a measurable cost that can make recovery-window optimization genuinely economic.

A narrow configuration optimizer can remain distinct from mature dunning if it does not send messages, retry payments or own billing; competition must be tested against configuration-intelligence features, not only dunning vendors.
For app-wide settings, causal attribution is a first-class gate because lack of per-user experimentation can weaken performance-fee pricing even when the decision is financially important.
